1: When I was a little child, dwelling in the kingdom of my Father's house, and enjoying the wealth and the splendours of those who reared me, my parents sent me forth from the East, our home, with a mission: down the road to Egypt, to fetch the one Pearl that lies in the midst of the sea, in the land of the devouring serpent.

They girded me with gold and precious stones; they clothed me in a purple robe, wrought with gold, and a garment of fine linen. And they wrote the covenant upon my heart: If you go down to Egypt and bring back the Pearl from the serpent, you shall put on again the robe and the garment, and with your brother, our next-heir, you shall be heir in our kingdom.

I left the East and went down, with two guardians to guide me — for the road was perilous and hard, and I was still a child, too small for the journey alone. I crossed the borders of the Maeonians, and I came to the land of Babel, and I entered the walls of Sarbug, and I went down into Egypt — and my companions parted from me.
2: And I found the serpent, and I settled near him, waiting until he should sleep so that I might take the Pearl. But while I was there, I forgot — I forgot that I was a son of kings, and I served their king. I forgot the Pearl for which my parents had sent me. And by the heaviness of their food, I fell into a deep sleep.

Then my parents, seeing in what distress I was, grieved for me, and the herald proclaimed in our country: The son of the king is perishing in Egypt. And they wrote me a letter, which every noble signed with his name: From your Father the King of kings, and your Mother the Mistress of the East, and your Brother our next-heir: Awake, sleeper, and rise from your slumber, and hear the words of our letter!
[Hymn of the Pearl 66-82 — The memory returns]

And it flew to me like an eagle, the king of all winged fowl, and it came and alighted beside me, and became all speech. At its voice and at the sound of its rustling I awoke and rose from my sleep, and I took it and kissed it, and I began to read. And as I read, I found written in it exactly what was written on my heart.
3: [Hymn of the Pearl 83-98 — The serpent charmed]

I remembered that I was a son of kings, and my noble birth asserted itself. I remembered the Pearl, for whose sake I was sent down to Egypt. I went to the serpent and charmed him, and lulled him to sleep by naming my Father's name over him. And I took the Pearl, and turned to carry it to my Father.
[Hymn of the Pearl 99-115 — The garments again]

And my splendrous robe, which I had stripped off, and my garment which I had put away — I saw them as I was journeying. Their beauty grew the more I saw it, woven of gold and precious stones, and every movement I made, it mirrored, until it seemed the robe moved of itself and was running toward me to meet me.

And I put on my robe, and I clothed myself in the garment, and I put it on, and I rose up, arrayed in it, for the heights of the world. And I returned and came near to the heavenly ones, and I came near to the gates of salutation and of peace, and I bowed my head to the King of kings who had sent it, for I had done His commandment, and He had done what He had promised.
